newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche declines comment, plans no statement.
newsitem.headline: Roche declines comment, plans no statement.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding AG said it had no comment on the latest flurry of rumours about the company and it was not planning to issue any statement during the day that could help explain why the share has risen so sharply.
"We have no comment on the rumours," a Roche spokesman said, repeating the company's policy of not comment on market rumours.
"We have no communique planned for today that could substantially explain the price jump," he added.
Roche certificates hit a new record high of 12,500 Swiss francs ($8,730) earlier in the day, a jump of 11.9 percent, but later eased and were up 585 francs, or 5.5 percent at 1200 GMT.
Turnover in Roche's non-voting equity securities (Genussscheine) was heavy on the Swiss Exchange.
Among the rumours swirling through the market was one that Roche could sell its fragrances business and this would give the company further cash to make a bid for another company.
Shares in British drug companies SmithKline Beecham and Zeneca rose in London on rumours that Roche might team up with a foreign company.
Other dealers speculated that a major player was hedging its positions in Roche in light of the strong rise in its stock, which could have caught some warrant issuers short of stock.
Swiss shares are often subject to so-called short-squeezes because of the amount of covered warrants in the Swiss market.
Following the announcement that Swiss pharma groups Sandoz AG and Ciba-Geigy AG would merge into Novartis, Roche's stock lost some of its glamour among investors.
During the second half of last year Roche's securities lost ground before bottoming out in late September.

Lately, however, analysts and investors have again warmed to Roche and last week's announcement that 1996 sales rose 11 percent to 15.96 billion Swiss francs confirmed to analysts that Roche was on track to boost 1996 profits by 15 percent.
The day after Roche issued its sales figures, Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB), for example, forecast a 25 percent upside in Roche's stock over the next 18 to 24 months.
-- Peter Nielsen, Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340 ($ = 1.431 Swiss Francs)
